title: ITS and LSU nrDNA analyses
author: Maria P Martin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wpdfdi6
materials: ITS and LSU nrDNA analyses Martín MP, Accioly T, Sousa JO, Roy M, Gardes M, Baseia IG Internal Transcribed Spacer (ITS) region of the nuclear ribosomal gene, including the 5.8S subunit (ITS nrDNA), the current barcoding of Fungi [1], and Large Subunit region of nuclear ribosomal DNA (LSU nrDNA) were the loci selected for molecular analyses. After DNA extraction, the ITS regions were amplified and sequenced using the primer pair ITS1F/ITS4 [2,3] for all samples. Part of the LSU was amplified and sequenced using either the primer pair LR0R/LR5 [4] for UFRN–Fungos, INPA-Fungos and CEPEC samples or the primer pair CTB6-TW14 [3] for the other samples. When amplifications were not obtained, nested PCR of ITS and semi-nested PCR of LSU were performed: first amplification with primers ITS1F/ITS4B [2] and LR0R/LR7 [4], and a second amplification with ITS5/ITS4 [3], and LR0R/LR5 or LR0R/LR4 [4]. Amplifications were done using illustraTM PureTaqTM Ready–To–GoTM PCR Beads (Healthcare, Buckinghamshire, UK), adding 1 µl at 10 µM of each primer and 23 µl (1.5–5.0 ng/µl) of isolated DNA, and cycling condition indicated in Martín and Winka [5]. Verification of amplification products was done on 1% agarose gels (UtraPureTM Invitrogen). Purification was done with ExoSAP–IT® (USB Corporation, OH, USA) and the samples were sequenced bidirectionally in Macrogen Inc. (Seoul, South Korea). Consensus sequences were obtained using Sequencher 5.2.4 (Gene Codes Corp., USA). Preliminary identifications were performed through megablast searches comparing the newly-generated sequences with those in GenBank [6]. Sequences obtained in this study were submitted to Genbank under the accession numbers indicated in Table 1.

steps.title: Gather and align ITS/LSU sequences
steps.instruction: Obtain the newly generated ITS and LSU sequences and retrieve homologous sequences from EMBL/GenBank/DDBJ; align the ITS sequences unambiguously before downstream analyses.

steps.title: Prepare concatenated ITS‑LSU dataset
steps.instruction: Create a concatenated ITS/LSU alignment that includes only specimens for which both ITS and LSU nrDNA sequences are available.

steps.title: Run Maximum Parsimony analysis
steps.instruction: Use PAUP* version 4.0a (build 159) for 32‑bit Windows to perform MP analysis on the aligned ITS dataset with the following settings: calculate minimum‑length Fitch trees by heuristic search using the Tree Bisection Reconnection (TBR) algorithm, collapse branches if maximum length is zero, enable the Multitrees option, start trees with 2 random stepwise additions, treat gaps as a new state, and perform 10,000 bootstrap replicates (MPbs). After tree search, obtain the consistency index (CI), retention index (RI), rescaled consistency index (RC), and homoplasy index (HI) for the 50 % majority‑rule consensus tree.

substeps.instruction: Launch PAUP* v4.0a (build 159) on Windows.
Set heuristic search = TBR, branch‑swapping = TBR, collapse branches if max length = 0, Multitrees = on.
Specify 2 random stepwise addition replicates.
Treat gaps as a new character state.
Run 10,000 bootstrap replicates.
Calculate CI, RI, RC, and HI for the 50 % majority‑rule consensus tree.

steps.title: Run Maximum Likelihood analysis
steps.instruction: Perform ML analysis with RAxML‑HPC‑2 on the CIPRES Science Gateway using Lewis ascertainment bias correction, 1,000 bootstrap replicates (MLbs), and the default GTRCAT model; then compute a 50 % majority‑rule consensus tree.

substeps.instruction: Access the CIPRES Science Gateway (http://www.phylo.org/).
Select RAxML‑HPC‑2 and upload the aligned ITS (or concatenated ITS/LSU) dataset.
Enable Lewis ascertainment bias correction.
Set number of bootstrap replicates to 1,000.
Use the default GTRCAT substitution model.
Run the analysis and generate a 50 % majority‑rule consensus tree.

steps.title: Run Bayesian phylogenetic analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct Bayesian inference with BEAST v2.4.7 (using BEAUti v2, LogCombiner v2.4.7, and TreeAnnotator v2.4.3) for both ITS alone and concatenated ITS/LSU datasets: create two independent runs of 50 million MCMC generations under the Yule speciation model, sampling every 5,000 generations; select the best‑fit substitution model for each marker with jModelTest 2; assess convergence with Tracer v1.7, discard burn‑in until the stationary phase, and summarize the post‑burn‑in trees as a Maximum Clade Credibility (MCC) tree.

substeps.instruction: Use BEAUti v2 to prepare BEAST XML files for each dataset (ITS alone and concatenated ITS/LSU).
For each dataset, set the tree prior to the Yule model of speciation.
Specify 50 000 000 MCMC generations and sampling every 5,000 generations.
Run two independent MCMC chains per dataset.
Determine the optimal substitution model for each marker with jModelTest 2 and apply it in the BEAST XML.
Execute the BEAST runs.
Load the resulting log files into Tracer v1.7 to verify convergence between runs.
Discard an appropriate burn‑in fraction until the stationary phase is reached.
Combine post‑burn‑in trees with LogCombiner v2.4.7 if needed.
Generate a Maximum Clade Credibility tree using TreeAnnotator v2.4.3.

steps.title: Visualize and edit phylogenetic trees
steps.instruction: Open the MP, ML, and Bayesian MCC trees in FigTree, edit and annotate them as needed, and finalize the figures in CorelDraw® Graphics Suite X8.

steps.title: Re‑analyze unsupported nodes with trimmed ITS
steps.instruction: For terminal nodes not supported by all three analyses, extract an ITS alignment containing only the morphologically ambiguous samples, trim sequence ends to remove short coverage, and repeat the Bayesian analysis in BEAST 2 using the same parameters as before; then obtain a new MCC tree for these samples.

substeps.instruction: Select the subset of samples requiring delimitation based on morphology.
Trim the ITS sequences at the 5′ and 3′ ends to eliminate short nucleotide coverage.
Create a new alignment with the trimmed sequences.
Prepare a BEAST XML with the same settings as the original Bayesian runs (Yule model, 50 million generations, sampling every 5,000 generations, model chosen by jModelTest 2).
Run the Bayesian analysis in BEAST 2.
Generate the MCC tree with TreeAnnotator.

steps.title: Create topo‑phylogeny and network visualizations
steps.instruction: Use the final MCC tree to produce a Topo‑Phylogeny representation (Waese et al.) and a phylogenetic network with SplitsTree4; finalize all artwork in CorelDraw® Graphics Suite X8.

substeps.instruction: Import the MCC tree into the Topo‑Phylogeny tool to generate a topographic landscape visualization.
Load the same tree into SplitsTree4 to construct a phylogenetic network.
Export the visualizations and refine them in CorelDraw® Graphics Suite X8 for publication.
